thread:
Ellen (SWE): Heads up team 1 I'll be relocating to Lisbon for 3 months on a workcation starting Aug 1. Do I need to change my homebase? Will benefits or pension be impacted for temporary EU stays?
Ravi (People Ops): Short answer: temporary moves under 90 days don't normally require a homebase change, but 3 months is near the threshold. Please fill the short-term relocation form so we can assess.
Ellen (SWE): Form submitted — what's the next step?
Cara (Payroll): Thanks Ellen. We need your estimated dates, local address while in Lisbon, and emergency contact. For temporary stays we document it but keep your US homebase unless stay exceeds 180 days or you establish residency. We'll check tax treaty implications.
Benefits Bot: Reminder  For international temporary relocations, benefits carriers will review. You may need to obtain temporary international coverage or file for travel health add-on. Employer pension contributions continue to your US plan unless you enroll in a local system.
Ellen (SWE): Any WFH stipend changes? I'm planning to keep my apartment in SF and pay for coworking in Lisbon.
Ravi (People Ops): Stipend continues for your declared homebase. We don't issue separate country-specific stipends. If you reimburse coworking, submit expenses through Concur with approval.
Ellen (SWE): Tax concerns for me personally?
Cara (Payroll): Short stays generally don't change US withholding; however, you may have local tax filing requirements in Portugal if you exceed certain days or earn Portuguese-source income. We recommended consulting a tax advisor. We'll also alert Global Mobility.
Ellen (SWE): OK thanks, I'll keep the dates under 90 days but will update if extended.
Ravi (People Ops): Sounds good. If extension looks likely, circle back 30 days before expiration so we can process a homebase change and benefits check.
Ellen (SWE): Will do :airplane:
